narration_timeline.text: Why do mallards often stay together as they move across a pond?
narration_timeline.scene: Visible group of mallards swimming together in an Oulu park.

narration_timeline.text: These ducks can swim in loose groups, turning along the bank as they travel.
narration_timeline.scene: Adult mallards moving on Ljubljana Prule waterway.

narration_timeline.text: At different waterways, mallards paddle past one another and keep exploring the shallow edges.
narration_timeline.scene: Two real mallard clips on different Ljubljana river dates.

narration_timeline.text: Their webbed feet carry them through water, while their bills help them search for food.
narration_timeline.scene: Mallards on a pond in Drage; webbed feet explained but not claimed visible.

narration_timeline.text: A group may spread out, then come close again as it travels across the pond.
narration_timeline.scene: Adult mallards moving in Ljubljana winter waterway.

narration_timeline.text: When ducklings are nearby, swimming close to family becomes part of that same daily journey.
narration_timeline.scene: Actual mallard ducklings near bank and separate USFWS adult-with-young footage.
